 With 'Fake Friday' weekend in full swing (despite the fact that the actual , official Black Friday event isn't 'til next week, on November 27), it's high time to take advantage of Black Friday deals to upgrade your listening gear.
 Whether its headphones or earbuds you're after (and feel free to take my headphone-finder quiz below, if you're still working that out) I'm here to help you make the most of this annual super-sale — and of course the gift-giving season directly after it.
 • See all of today's best early Black Friday deals 
 Top of the headphone deals pile for me in the US? Simple: The Bose headphones below only arrived in August 2026 and they've already got this whopping discount — even in the limited-edition green colorways.
 Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen): was $359 now $199 at Amazon 
 And since we're here, a close second would be the excellent Nothing cans below, which are an absolute steal at this lowest-seen price.
 Nothing Headphone (a) : was $199 now $109 at Amazon 
 Across the pond in the UK? It's quite a different scene, but this is what I see in the top spot: CMF by Nothing Headphone Pro: was £79 now £49 at Amazon 
 As I say, Black Friday proper isn't quite here yet, but since when has that stopped huge online retailers in the Internet age? What I'm saying is, many Black Friday headphones deals are already live, and there are some serious savings — especially on more premium products.
 Interestingly, some deals have really started early in one country (UK, I'm looking at you) but not others, so we've seen a ton of savings on Nothing, Bose and Sony cans, but similar deals have yet to land in the US yet. That being said, I've seen one especially good Bose deal in the US that hasn't made it to the UK so far. I'd expect that to change pretty soon, though.

The best Black Friday audio deals of 2026 - SoundGuys

 The best Black Friday audio deals of 2026
 The Black Friday deals on headphones, earbuds and speakers that are worth your money
 Adam Birney 
 •
 Nov 20, 2026 — 4:38 PM ET 
 •
 •

 Preferred Source Google Discover 
 Black Friday is when the headphones you’ve had sitting in your cart since summer finally drop to a price you can live with. It’s also when every retailer insists a $10 markdown is the deal of the year, and telling the two apart is half the battle. We test audio gear for a living, so we’ve dug through this year’s sales to find the discounts on headphones, earbuds and speakers that are worth your money.
 Whether you’re upgrading your own setup or crossing names off a gift list, these are the deals we’d point our friends to. We’ll keep adding to this list as new deals land through Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Prices can shift fast this time of year, so double-check the price at checkout.
 Ozlo Sleepbuds 2 for $239 ($40 off)
 Promoted 
 Ozlo Sleepbuds 2 
 Ozlo Sleepbuds 2 MSRP: $279.00 
 The Ozlo Sleepbuds 2 are compact earbuds designed for overnight use, with a low-profile shape suited to side sleeping. They offer up to 14 hours of battery life, built-in ambient sounds, Bluetooth audio, sleep tracking, and improved initial pairing compared with the original model.
 See price at Ozlo 
 Save $40.00 
 See price at Amazon 
 From November 19 to 30, the Ozlo Sleepbuds 2 are $239 at Ozlo, down from $279, and every order comes with a free surprise holiday gift. Ozlo calls them the world’s smallest earbuds designed just for sleep, and they’re built to stay comfortable all night, even for side sleepers. In our review, they sat flush enough that rolling over in bed didn’t push them into our ears, and after eight hours of streaming they still had about 30% battery left, with Ozlo rating them for up to 14 hours. Ozlo’s private alarm plays only in your ears, so it wakes you without waking anyone beside you, and you can snooze it with the button on the case. Overnight, the earbuds and case track your sleep along with room noise, light, and temperature, so you can see what shapes your rest. This is its lowest price of the year and a great time to grab a premium pair of earbuds for sleeping.
 Beats Studio Pro for $139.95 (53% off)
 Beats Studio Pro 
 Beats Studio Pro Enhanced smartphone integration • Lossless and Spatial Audio • Big battery life
 MSRP: $349.00 
 Spatial audio, lossless playback, and big battery life
 The Beats Studio Pro are a relatively light-weight set of Bluetooth headphones. With up to 40 hours of battery life, USB Type-C charging and wired playback, as well as a 3.5mm port, ANC, and Spatial Audio, these are contenders for the hottest headphones of 2023.
 See price at Amazon 
 The Beats Studio Pro drop to $139.95 in Amazon-exclusive Light Blue. In our testing they lasted 31 hours and 25 minutes on a charge, and with a good seal their ANC cut most commuting noise by 50–90%. You can also listen wired over USB-C or a 3.5mm cable. The catch is fit: the small ear cups made them uncomfortable for our reviewer within an hour, so glasses-wearers and anyone with a larger head should look elsewhere.
 Bose QuietComfort Headphones for $169 (53% off)
 Bose QuietComfort Headphones 
 Bose QuietComfort Headphones Great battery life • Comfortable materials • Great ANC
 MSRP: $349.00 
 Comfortable cans with next-level noise cancellation and great battery life
 The Bose QuietComfort Headphones focus on your comfort and listening experience in noisy environments. Enjoy up to 24 hours of battery life and Bose's high-quality sound in a plush set of new wireless headphones.
 See price at Amazon 
 The Bose QuietComfort Headphones are down to $169 . Comfort is their strong suit, and their ANC reduced engine and street noise by 50–85% in our tests, with 27 hours and 14 minutes of battery per charge. We didn’t think they were worth $349 because the default sound is bass-heavy and Bose’s app offers only a basic three-band EQ. At less than half that, they’re an easier buy for frequent flyers who want a comfortable pair for long trips.
 Beats Solo 4 for $99.95 (50% off)
 Beats Solo 4 
 Beats Solo 4 Spatial Audio with head tracking • Color options • Battery life
 MSRP: $199.00 
 Some sequels just aren't worth the hype.
 This is not the set of headphones you buy because you want bang for your buck. There are a very narrow range of needs these headphones suit, and you'd be better served waiting for these to go on sale before considering them.
 See price at Amazon 
 The Beats Solo 4 are $99.95 , half their $199.95 list price. Battery life is the standout: they ran for 84 hours and 18 minutes in our test, and you can listen wired over USB-C or 3.5mm when they do run flat. There’s no ANC or transparency mode, though, and the on-ear fit let in a lot of outside noise and pressed on our reviewer’s ears after an hour and a half. We told readers not to pay full price, so this deal suits iPhone owners who want a light, foldable pair with head-tracked Spatial Audio.
 JLab JBuds Lux ANC for $48.99 (51% off)
 JLab JBuds Lux ANC 
 JLab JBuds Lux ANC USB-C audio • Sound quality • Comfort
 MSRP: $79.99 
 For under $100, these are crazy good value.
 As far as inexpensive ANC headphones go, the JLab JBuds Lux ANC are one of the best of 2024. They focus on the fundamentals, and not fighting the spec wars.
 See price at Amazon 
 See price at Best Buy 
 The JLab JBuds Lux ANC are $48.99 , which is a lot of headphone for under $50. They lasted 44 hours and 22 minutes in our battery test, support wired listening over USB-C, and JLab’s app includes a 10-band EQ. Their ANC is modest, reducing low-frequency noise by 50–75%, but the thick padding is comfortable for hours and works well with glasses. There’s no IP rating, so keep them out of the gym.
 Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro for $179.99 (28% off)
 Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro 
 Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro Head gesture support • Improved ANC • Distinctive design
 MSRP: $249.00 
 Samsung's top Galaxy Buds get a welcome refresh
 The Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro brings a redesigned look, along with improved ANC, head gesture support, and more seamless AI smarts.
 See price at Amazon 
 Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro 
 The Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro are $179.99 , $70 off Samsung’s flagship earbuds. Their ANC reduced outside noise by an average of 84% in our lab, they carry an IP57 rating, and they support Auracast. Battery life is short at 6 hours and 1 minute per charge, and there’s no true multipoint. Features like Samsung’s high-quality codec and ultra-wideband calls need a recent Galaxy phone, so this deal is really for Samsung owners.
 Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 for $124.95 (31% off)
 Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 
 Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 Leaves ears open • Bluetooth 5.3 • IP55 rating
 MSRP: $179.95 
 The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 are the cream of the crop when it comes to bone conduction headphones.
 The top bone conduction earbuds from Shokz deliver extensive features including Bluetooth 5.3, IP55 rating, and a companion app with an EQ.
 See price at Amazon 
 The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 are $124.95 . These bone conduction headphones rest on your cheekbones and leave your ears open, so you can hear traffic on a run. This generation adds louder bass, USB-C charging, Bluetooth multipoint and a five-band EQ in the Shokz app, and Shokz rates them for 12 hours per charge. Our reviewer found the microphone weak in wind, and the IP55 rating is lower than the cheaper OpenRun’s.
 Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) for $99 (38% off)
 Bose Soundlink Flex (2nd Gen) 
 Bose Soundlink Flex (2nd Gen) IP67 • Rugged build • Strap attachment
 MSRP: $149.00 
 Same Flex, newer tech.
 While the SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) doesn't offer any major hardware upgrades over its predecessor, it does feature some helpful updates. Whether you're camping in the rain or enjoying a sunny afternoon at the beach, the SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) remains a solid choice for a portable, durable Bluetooth speaker that can handle the great outdoors.
 See price at Amazon 
 The Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) is $99 in limited-edition colors. It’s an IP67-rated speaker with a strap loop, multipoint, and aptX on Snapdragon Sound phones, and you can pair two for stereo. It lasted 7 hours and 3 minutes in our battery test, short of Bose’s 12-hour claim. The default sound is safe, but a quick bass and treble boost in the Bose app livens it up.
 Sony ULT Field 1 for $68 (51% off)
 Sony ULT Field 1 
 Sony ULT Field 1 Durable • Portable • Lightweight
 MSRP: $129.00 
 See price at Amazon 
 The Sony ULT Field 1 is $68 in Smoke Blue, and the deal includes a $15 Amazon gift card. It’s a light, IP67-rated speaker that Sony says survives a 4-foot drop, and it lasted 28 hours and 45 minutes in our test with ULT mode off. Turn ULT on for fuller bass, since the speaker sounds thin without it. It’s mono, and the Sony app’s three-band EQ can’t adjust ULT mode.
 Marshall Emberton III for $89.99 (50% off)
 Marshall Emberton III 
 Marshall Emberton III MSRP: $169.00 
 See price at Manufacturer site 
 The Marshall Emberton III is $89.99 , half its $179.99 list price. We haven’t put it through our lab yet. Marshall rates it for more than 32 hours of playback and IP67 dust and water resistance, with two 10W full-range drivers. It also adds a microphone for hands-free calls, which the Emberton II lacked.
 Sonos Arc Ultra for $849 (23% off)
 Sonos Arc Ultra soundbar + Sub 4 subwoofer 
 Sonos Arc Ultra soundbar + Sub 4 subwoofer Sleek design • Sub performance • HDMI eARC connection
 MSRP: $1,798.00 
 The Sonos Arc Ultra + Sub 4 deliver sleek looks, deep bass, and solid performance for home.
 The Sonos Arc Ultra + Sub 4 combines premium design with powerful sound. It’s a streamlined home theater setup with strong bass and easy app control, though the price may give some pause.
 See price at Amazon 
 The Sonos Arc Ultra is $849 , $250 off. We tested it with the Sub 4, which isn’t part of this deal, and found it sounds great on its own, with a 9.1.4-channel layout and full Dolby Atmos over HDMI eARC. Trueplay tuning in the Sonos app calibrates it to your room in a few minutes. It’s 46 inches long and has no optical port or extra HDMI inputs, so it suits TVs 55 inches and up.
